 Judgment
This is claimants appeal for enhancement of compensation and praying to direct respondent/insurer to pay the compensation and recover it from the owner of the vehicle.
2. The parties will be referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal, for sake of convenience.

Brief facts of the case is as under:
4.

It is the case of the claimants that on 21/02/2018, one Mr.Nagareddy was going towards Humnabad by walk on the left side of the road; near Basanthpur village, on NH50,
Humnabad-Kalburgi Road, he met with an accident due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-32- EN-1186 by its driver.
As a result of the impact, the deceased - Nagareddy sustained grievous injuries.

He was shifted to Government Hospital, Humnabad for treatment and while undergoing treatment, he succumbed to the injuries on the same day at 5.30 p.m.
5.
It is further case of the claimants that they are the legal representatives and depends of the deceased - Nagareddy.
The deceased - Nagareddy was aged about 55 years at the time of accident and he was agriculturist and earning Rs.15,000/- per NC: 2024:KHC-K:3827 month.
With these reasons, they claimed to award compensation of Rs.29,30,000/-.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2/insurer denied contents of the claim petition.
It was further contended that rider of the motorcycle had no valid and effective driving license.
Therefore, respondents are not liable to pay compensation.
With these reasons, prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
7. From the rival contentions of both the parties, the Tribunal had framed the necessary issues for its determination.
8. The claimants were examined PWs.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P1 to 7 and closed their evidence.

The respondent No.2 has examined RW-1 and got marked Ex.D1 and D1(a).
9.

The Tribunal after hearing both the parties and appreciating the evidence available on record had awarded the following amount of compensation:-

1. Loss of dependency (Rs.8000+10%X12-1\4X11) Rs.8,71,200/-
2. Lose of consortium Rs.40,000/-
3. Lose of estate Rs.15,000/-
4.

Funeral expenses, obsequies and Transportation of dead Rs.15,000/-
body etc.
I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for both the parties.

11. The learned counsel for appellants submits that deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
However, the Tribunal has taken income only Rs.8,000/- p.m. which is on lower side.

As per the chart of income prepared by the KSLSA, Accordingly, notional income could be fixed at Rs.11,750/-
p.m.

The amount of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium is also on lower side and not in accordance with law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex NC: 2024:KHC-K:3827 Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others1.

sentences.text: Therefore, prayed for enhancement of compensation.
12. It is further submitted by the learned advocate for petitions that the Tribunal has held that rider of the motorcycle had no valid and affective driving license.
However, respondents have not challenged charge sheet filed by the Police and hence, the said reasons assigned by the Tribunal cannot be considered.

He further submits that in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Pappu And Others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba And Another2, insurance company be directed to pay the compensation and recover the same from the respondent No.1.
13.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that there is no reasons to interfere with the (2018) 18 SCC 130 2018 ACJ 690 NC: 2024:KHC-K:3827 findings of Trial Court.

The rider of the Mallamma And Ors vs Anilkumar And Anr on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130517400/
3 motorcycle had no valid and effective driving license to ride the motorcycle and it is rightly considered by the Trial Court and exonerated insurance company from the liability to pay the compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has further submitted that Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.6154/2019 dated 14.12.2023, held that in case of failure of the rider of the vehicle, holding a valid driving license, the Insurance Company cannot be made liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the law laid down by the Division Bench of this Court, the contention of the appellants shall not be considered.
There is no need to interference in the findings of trial Court.

With these reasons,
prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
14. The following questions arise for my determination.
i. "Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation.?
Whether respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle?."
15. Fact of accident and death of Nagareddy due to accident are not seriously disputed.
No need to reconsider the same.
16. There is no reliable evidence produced by the claimants to accept the income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Tribunal had taken notional income at Rs.8,000/-p.m.
The submission of learned advocate for appellant in this regard acceptable.

17. As per the chart the notional income of the deceased could be as Rs.11750/- p.m.,
18.
There is no dispute in respect of addition of future prospects, multiplier or deduction towards personal expenses.
Accordingly, the compensation is re-
calculated.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited (Supra) Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded towards loss of consortium to each of the claimants.
The Tribunal has awarded just compensation under the head funeral expenses and loss of estate.
Hence no need of enhancement.
Accordingly, following amount of compensation is awarded.

1. Loss of dependency Rs.8,71,200/- Rs.12,79,575/-
 2. Loss of consortium Rs.40,000/- Rs.1,60,000/-
 3. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 4.

Funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-

sentences.text: The claimants are entitled for enhancement of Rs.5,28,375/-.
Accordingly, question number one is partly answered in favour of the claimants.
The Tribunal after considering the evidence on record, held that rider of the motorcycle had no valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
The said findings does not call for any interference.
Appellants have not produced the driving license of the rider of the motorcycle even before this Court.
Hence, it is not proved that rider of vehicle had no valid licence to ride the vehicle.
22. The contract of Insurance is between owner and insurer, the third party are not concerned with the conditions of insurance of policy.
The owner committed default in permitting an unauthorized person to ride the vehicle.
Under these circumstances, insurance company shall pay compensation and it may recover the compensation from owner of the vehicle.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case Pappu (supra) as well as in the case of Mukund Dewangan V/s.

Oriental Insurance - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3827 Company Limited3, it is held that in case of violation of conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company has to pay the compensation to third party and recover it from the insured.
In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court the insurer has to pay compensation to claimants and recover it from insured.
In view of the above said judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court the judgment of Division Bench in MFA No.6154/2019, is not applicable to this case.
Accordingly, question No.2 is answered in negative.

23. Accordingly, I pass the following;
O RD E R i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
